sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: April 23, 2026 announcement releases GPT-5.5 in ChatGPT and Codex; an April 24 update confirms API availability. It describes reasoning, coding, visual computer use and tools. Codex launch context was 400K, distinct from API limits. Serving-hardware and load-balancing details do not disclose neural parameter counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model page identifies default snapshot gpt-5.5-2026-04-23, text/image input, text output, 1,050,000 context, 128,000 max output, reasoning none/low/medium/high/xhigh with medium default, Chat Completions and Responses, function calling, computer use and explicit prompt caching.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Original April 23 card updated April 24 describes data and reinforcement-learning reasoning training. It explicitly identifies Pro as the same underlying model using parallel test-time compute. Full text contains no numerical total/active production parameters or detailed block composition.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: July 9 card, including August updates, has exact GPT-5.5 columns for safety, vision, destructive-action avoidance, health and biology evaluations. The separate GPT-5.5 and Pro columns and corrected pass@4 values are evaluation metrics, not model sizes. No GPT-5.5 production parameter or architecture disclosure was found in its full extracted text.

sources.title: Self-replicating prompt injections exist
sources.evidence: September 25 research explicitly uses GPT-5.5 as both vulnerable model and attack discoverer in a separate Slack evaluation with the Codex harness. GPT-5.4-mini-derived internal checkpoints are separately identified. No GPT-5.5 total/active counts or neural structure are disclosed.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: July 29 summary identifies GPT-5.5 as neither a modification nor a fine-tune of a previous model, with Union-market placement April 23. It describes training-data quantities and modalities, including audiovisual sources represented partly as transcripts/captions. These are not production parameters or API audio/video capability. No network structure/count is disclosed.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived technical guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6 and describes OpenAI prompt caching through Transformer attention key/value projections. Combined with exact GPT-5.5 caching support this supports only a broad qualified Transformer inference.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses PDF processing for vision-capable models extracts text and page images; Chat Completions also accepts PDFs. This supports PDF as an API document format alongside the exact model vision and endpoint support, not an additional native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: April 24 explicitly releases GPT-5.5 to Chat Completions and Responses, with medium-default reasoning and extended prompt caching only. June 1 Bedrock expansion is later provider availability, not the original release.

sources.title: Model Release Notes
sources.evidence: October 14 retirement removes GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex and explicitly does not affect API access.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: Current complete page checked for exact gpt-5.5 and its dated snapshot; no exact API shutdown notice found. Documentation alone is not an endpoint operation test.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 provide limited hosted-service access and reserve service intellectual-property ownership, supporting descriptive Proprietary classification rather than a downloadable-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: GPT-5.5 is listed among hosted models, distinct from the Open-weight section naming Apache-licensed gpt-oss models. Checked exact release and inventory offer no downloadable GPT-5.5 weights.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.5 record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead inspected via raw file; its generic family and promotional description are not treated as primary proof. Context, date and capabilities were independently checked.

name.note: Official model name; Thinking is its ChatGPT presentation, distinct from GPT-5.5 Instant.

developer.note: Developer named in original release and technical publications.

family.note: Normalize to the named generation; no transfer of sibling counts or capabilities.

release_date.note: Earliest public ChatGPT/Codex release. API release followed April 24 even though its snapshot is dated April 23. Union-market date corroborates April 23.

open_weights.note: Hosted distribution under reserved service IP; no downloadable weights in the checked official release and model inventory.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service classification, not SPDX or an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No numerical production total in original card, later exact-model comparisons, exact-model research or public training summary. Targeted parameter, training and interpretability searches found no disclosure. Training tokens, hardware capacities and benchmark metrics are not model parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active count or activation topology disclosed in these original/later exact-model sources. Do not equate active and total or infer dense/MoE layout.

architecture.note: Qualified inference from exact prompt-caching feature and pre-GPT-5.6 Transformer KV explanation. This is a broad classification only; checked original/later technical and training evidence does not establish full block composition, dense/MoE topology or layer counts.

context_window.note: Exact API total context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output. Do not derive a separate input ceiling by subtraction. Codex launch limit was 400K; product limits differ. No endpoint operation test.

modalities.note: Native text/image inputs and text output. PDF is an API format converted into extracted text and page images. Training audiovisual sources do not imply exposed audio/video support; hosted image generation is a tool, not native output.

reasoning.note: Exact API supports reasoning tokens and none, low, medium, high and xhigh effort; medium is default. Original card describes RL reasoning training.

tool_call.note: Exact model supports function calling and tools including computer use; no sibling inference.

description.value: OpenAI reasoning model for coding and general tasks, with text and image input, tool calling and computer use.
description.note: Replace unsupported current-default and promotional framing with documented purpose and capabilities.

sources.label: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5

patch.notes: Released April 23, 2026 in ChatGPT and Codex; API release followed April 24, with default snapshot gpt-5.5-2026-04-23. API context is 1,050,000 tokens with a 128,000-token output limit; Codex launch context was 400K. PDF denotes API extraction into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified broad inference from exact prompt-caching support and OpenAI pre-GPT-5.6 KV-cache documentation; full topology and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked sources. The public training summary describes data quantities, not model size or exposed audio/video support. October 14 retirement from ChatGPT, Work and Codex explicitly does not affect API access. No exact API shutdown notice was found; live endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirmed April 23 public release, April 24 API launch, 1.05M API context, reasoning, tools and text/image/PDF semantics. Corrected family, proprietary licensing, qualified Transformer architecture and description. Counts remain undisclosed after original and later exact-model sources, including the public training summary. Product retirement is distinct from API availability.
